application.route: Train, Judgement Puzzles notes board (desktop 1366, phone 390)

component: Toolbar density: nine equal icon buttons replaced by four direct controls and one grouped options menu
explanation: CaissaTrainer Phase 2 (training-notes.md N6 to N9). Observed: nine same weight icon buttons in one row, the ninth clipped by the panel edge, most used rarely, one (annotation symbols) opening a hidden 19 symbol grid. Rule applied: frequency decides visibility. At most about four direct controls per small tool; the rest live in one grouped menu button with a visible word on the trigger (Options, accessible name Notes board options), groups labelled (Position, Board, Annotate move), full APG menu button pattern (open with Enter, Space or ArrowDown; arrows, Home, End wrap; Escape closes and returns focus; Tab closes; click outside closes), items that cannot act are disabled with a reason, 36px targets with a precise pointer and 40px under a coarse pointer. Every function was preserved. P10 (minimalism over prevalence) covers the direction but gives no number and no grouping or menu button rule. Related: the workspace rail options menu (see the rail issue) uses the same pattern, and a shared menu button preset would serve both.

classification.rationale: P10 states the direction (fewer visible controls) but not a threshold or the grouped menu button pattern. Gap or ambiguity at the margin; the count of 4 is a judgement the owner must set. Owner confirmation needed.
